[← Back to the lesson: Logits](../logits.qmd)

## Check your understanding

1. If the vocabulary contains $V$ tokens, how many components does the logit vector contain at one position?

<details>
<summary>Show answer</summary>

It contains $V$ components, one for each vocabulary token.

</details>

2. Why does a logit with value 8 not mean an 80% probability?

<details>
<summary>Show answer</summary>

A logit is an unnormalized real-valued score. It is neither bounded between 0 and 1 nor constrained to sum to one. A separate transformation is needed to obtain a probability distribution.

</details>

3. What does the argmax of a logit vector identify?

<details>
<summary>Show answer</summary>

It identifies the token with the highest score in that vector. By itself, it does not measure confidence or truth.

</details>

4. Compare $z=(2,1)$ and $z'=(102,101)$. The logits are much larger in the second vector. Is the softmax distribution different? Why?

<details>
<summary>Show answer</summary>

No. The second vector is obtained by adding the same constant (100) to every component. This offset cancels in the softmax formula, so both vectors produce the same distribution. The absolute level of logits therefore has no standalone meaning; their differences matter.

</details>
